venues.name: Ananda in the Himalayas
venues.note: India's first destination spa and one of the world's greatest, a 100-acre Maharaja's estate above the Ganges, built for Ayurveda, yoga and genuine transformation.
credentials: Repeatedly ranked among the world's best destination spas

venues.name: Taj Rishikesh Resort & Spa, Uttarakhand
venues.area: Singthali Village (river road, ~30 km from town)
venues.note: A dramatic Himalayan-village resort on a private stretch of the Ganges, Taj polish, a 20,000 sq ft wellness sanctuary and a private river beach.
credentials: Taj Hotels luxury resort, 79 rooms, suites and villas (several with private pools)
Listed in the MICHELIN Guide (hotels)
Jiva Grande Spa and a 20,000 sq ft wellness sanctuary

venues.name: The Westin Resort & Spa, Himalayas
venues.note: Marriott's Himalayan debut, a wellness-led resort of valley-view rooms, infinity pools and yoga-inspired programming near the world's yoga capital.
credentials: The Westin's first Himalayan resort (Marriott Bonvoy)
141 rooms including royal garden villas with private pools
Built around Westin's six pillars of well-being; Heavenly Spa

venues.name: The Roseate Ganges, Rishikesh
venues.note: A design-led boutique retreat of 16 standalone villas on the Ganges, quiet, intimate and beautifully made, with a 17-metre infinity pool over the valley.
credentials: Roseate Hotels & Resorts luxury boutique retreat, 16 villas
Featured by Sleeper Magazine for its design
Aheli spa; 17m infinity pool over the Garhwal foothills

venues.name: EllBee Ganga View
venues.note: A boutique art hotel beside the Ganga at Triveni Ghat, rooms above the river, art on every wall and the evening aarti a short walk along the ghat.
credentials: Boutique art hotel on the Ganga at Triveni Ghat
Home to The Sitting Elephant rooftop restaurant
Steps from the Triveni Ghat Ganga Aarti

venues.name: Ananda in the Himalayas, cuisine
venues.note: Wellness cuisine at its most considered, Ayurvedic and calorie-conscious menus built around your programme, without ever feeling like a compromise.
credentials: Dining within India's most awarded destination spa
Menus overseen by in-house Ayurvedic doctors and nutritionists
Repeat Condé Nast Traveller World's Best Destination Spa standing

venues.name: Riverside, Taj Rishikesh
venues.note: Himalayan home cooking done properly, Kashmiri, Himachali, Garhwali, Kumaoni and Nepali classics, with the Ganges below.
credentials: Signature restaurant of Taj Rishikesh Resort & Spa
MICHELIN Guide (hotels) property
Focus on the food of the Himalayan states

venues.name: The Sitting Elephant, EllBee Ganga View
venues.note: A rooftop table over the Ganga at Triveni Ghat, multi-cuisine vegetarian cooking with the best old-town river view in Rishikesh.
credentials: Rooftop restaurant of the EllBee Ganga View boutique hotel
Panoramic Ganga and Triveni Ghat views
A recognised old-town dining name

venues.name: Little Buddha Café
venues.note: Rishikesh's most-loved café, a quirky treehouse of rooftop tables over the Ganga, a fixture of the town's traveller culture since 2007.
credentials: A landmark Rishikesh café (est. 2007)
Consistently ranked among the city's best cafés (Tripadvisor / Tripoto)
Celebrated riverside rooftop views by Laxman Jhula

venues.name: Bistro Nirvana
venues.note: The town's most polished café cooking, well-made Continental, Indian and Middle Eastern plates a notch above the traveller-café norm.
credentials: A recognised Rishikesh café (Tripoto / Himalayan Yoga Association)
Noted for well-executed international vegetarian dishes

venues.name: Chotiwala
venues.note: A Rishikesh institution of decades, thali-style pure-vegetarian cooking that still pulls pilgrims and locals to the old town.
credentials: A long-standing Rishikesh heritage eatery (decades-old)
A recognised old-town institution near Ram Jhula / Swarg Ashram

venues.name: The Ganga Aarti at Parmarth Niketan
venues.note: At dusk the largest ashram in Rishikesh gathers hundreds on the marble steps below its giant Shiva statue, and children of the ashram lead the fire prayer to the Ganga in unison, lamps, chanting and the river turning gold. It is the most soulful half-hour in town, and it is free. A private guide can secure a seat close to the priests and time your arrival before the crowd fills the ghat.

venues.name: The Maha Aarti at Triveni Ghat
venues.note: The grander, busier evening aarti, the town's main bathing ghat where the Ganga, Yamuna and mythic Saraswati are said to meet, ringed by lamplight and thousands of floating diyas. Rawer and more local than Parmarth, it is the fuller picture of a living pilgrim city. Come 30 minutes early; a guide keeps a multi-generation group together through the press.

venues.name: Lakshman Jhula & Ram Jhula (the swaying footbridges)
venues.note: The two iconic iron suspension bridges over the Ganga are the postcard of Rishikesh, pilgrims, cows, motorbikes and monkeys crossing above the green rush of the river. The century-old Lakshman Jhula has been closed and is being rebuilt, so the walkable pair today are Ram Jhula and the newer Janki Setu. Cross at first light before the heat and the crowds, then take chai on the far bank.

venues.name: Janki Setu (the newest glass-floor footbridge)
venues.note: The third and newest of the Ganga suspension bridges, with a glass-panel section and an evening light show that draws an easy crowd, a gentle, safe cross for grandparents and children while the older Lakshman Jhula stays shut. Temple bells and river chants carry from both banks. Best at blue hour when the lights come on.

venues.name: Parmarth Niketan (the ashram itself)
venues.note: Beyond the aarti, the largest ashram in Rishikesh is a serene 1,000-room riverside campus of gardens, temples and a daily rhythm of yoga and satsang, the spiritual centre of the yoga capital. A private darshan and a quiet dawn walk before the day begins is a gentle introduction to ashram life without committing to a stay.

venues.name: Swarg Ashram & the ashram belt
venues.note: The traffic-free heart of spiritual Rishikesh, a riverside warren of ashrams, temples, book stalls and Gita Bhawan's scripture library, where you can walk barefoot along the Ganga with temple bells for a soundtrack. This is where the yoga-and-meditation world actually lives. An early-morning walk with a guide who knows which ashrams welcome visitors is the way in.

venues.name: A private yoga & meditation session on the Ganga
venues.note: Rishikesh is where modern yoga went global, and a one-to-one dawn practice with a serious teacher on a riverside terrace, pranayama, asana, then silence as the mist lifts off the water, is the reason to come. Far more restorative than a group class. Your advisor can match teacher to level, from a first-timer to a lifelong practitioner.
credentials: Rishikesh is widely called the Yoga Capital of the World, an informal but universally used title

venues.name: Ananda in the Himalayas
venues.note: One of the world's great destination spas, a 100-acre estate around a Maharaja's palace high in the foothills, with Ganga views, Ayurvedic doctors, and week-long wellness programmes blending Ayurveda, yoga and Vedanta with international therapies. The ultra-luxury benchmark for the region and, for many, the whole reason to visit. Book a structured programme, not just nights, for the full effect.
credentials: Repeatedly ranked among the world's best destination spas

venues.name: The Vashishta Gufa (meditation cave)
venues.note: A sixty-foot natural cave where the sage Vashishta is said to have meditated, ending in a Shiva lingam in total darkness, you sit on the mud floor in pitch black and silence, with a small ashram and a quiet Ganga beach just outside. The most profound meditation spot near Rishikesh, and utterly uncrowded. A short drive up the Badrinath road; go mid-morning.

venues.name: The Flying Fox & cliff jumping
venues.note: A one-kilometre zip-line that flings you across the river valley at speed, and cliff-jumping into deep Ganga pools at Shivpuri, the fun, lower-commitment end of Rishikesh adventure for a mixed-age group. Best paired with a morning raft. Book through one operator so the day flows and the safety cover is real.

venues.name: The Tera Manzil (Trimbakeshwar) Temple
venues.note: A striking thirteen-storey riverside temple, 'Tera Manzil' means thirteen floors, packed with shrines to countless deities, its terraces climbing above the Ganga to a top-floor view over the bridges and the town. A vivid, colourful hour and a favourite photo spot. Climb barefoot in the cool of the morning.

venues.name: The Bharat Mandir
venues.note: The oldest temple in Rishikesh, said to have been established by Adi Shankaracharya, tucked in the bazaar lanes of the old town with a black-stone Vishnu idol and a quiet, unhurried atmosphere far from the tourist bridges. A short, grounding stop that most visitors miss. Best combined with a wander through the old-town markets.
credentials: The oldest temple in Rishikesh, traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya

venues.name: The cafes of Tapovan
venues.note: The hillside above Lakshman Jhula is a warren of rooftop cafes serving good coffee, wood-fired pizza, Israeli and Tibetan food and fresh juice, most with a Ganga view and a slow, barefoot, post-yoga rhythm. The town's social heart between practice sessions. Late afternoon, with the river below and the hills going pink, is the moment.

venues.name: Sattvic dining (the meat-and-alcohol-free town)
venues.note: Rishikesh and Haridwar are holy towns where meat, eggs, alcohol, and even garlic and onion in strict kitchens, are set aside for pure sattvic food: simple, fresh, vegetarian, cooked to nourish the practice. For a Jain or vegetarian traveller the whole destination is effortless. A private table at an ashram thali or a Tapovan cafe shows the range, from austere to genuinely delicious.
credentials: A legally alcohol- and meat-free holy town

venues.name: The Neer Garh Waterfall trek
venues.note: A short, pretty forest walk off the Tapovan road climbs past tiered limestone falls to a couple of clear plunge pools where you can cool off, the most accessible of the local waterfalls and an easy morning for a family. Go September to November when the monsoon has filled it. Carry water shoes.

venues.name: Riverside luxury camping at Shivpuri
venues.note: White-sand Ganga beaches upriver where premium camps pitch furnished tents by the water, bonfires, star fields, birdcall and a raft run at the door, without the roadside crowds of the town. A magical night for a multi-generation group who want the river without roughing it. Your advisor picks the camp with the beach and the standards to match.

venues.name: The Har Ki Pauri Ganga Aarti (Haridwar)
venues.note: The grandest Ganga aarti in the country, at Haridwar's holiest ghat, where Vishnu is said to have left a footprint, thousands gather at dusk as giant flaming lamps are swung to roaring bells and the river carries a carpet of leaf-boat diyas downstream. Overwhelming and unforgettable. A guide arranges a safe raised vantage away from the densest crush, essential with elders or children.
credentials: Haridwar's holiest ghat and the principal Kumbh Mela bathing site

venues.name: The Mansa Devi Ropeway (Haridwar)
venues.note: A cable-car ('udan khatola') swings up the hill to the wish-fulfilling Mansa Devi temple, with the whole spread of Haridwar and the Ganga laid out below, the fast, comfortable alternative to the 3-km climb and a highlight for children. Pair it with the Chandi Devi ropeway across the valley. Go mid-morning after the aarti crowds thin.

venues.name: The Kumbh Mela ground at Haridwar
venues.note: Har Ki Pauri is one of the four sites of the Kumbh Mela, the largest human gathering on earth, when tens of millions come to bathe, and even on an ordinary day a guide can tell the story on the very steps where it unfolds. Context that turns a river ghat into history. The next Haridwar Kumbh falls in 2033.
credentials: Site of the Kumbh Mela, among the largest human gatherings on Earth

venues.name: The gateway to the Char Dham Yatra
venues.note: Rishikesh and Haridwar are the traditional starting point of the Char Dham, the Himalayan pilgrimage to Yamunotri, Gangotri, Kedarnath and Badrinath, and even without the full circuit, a curated first leg up the Alaknanda valley to Devprayag and beyond gives a taste of the sacred road. The classic Indian spiritual journey begins here. Your advisor can shape a comfortable multi-day itinerary or a single scenic day out.

venues.name: A sunrise Ganga boat & morning dip
venues.note: Before the town wakes, a small boat drifts you across still, mist-hung water while pilgrims take their dawn dip and temple bells start up on both banks, the Ganga at its most peaceful, a world away from the raft crowds. The quietest, most contemplative hour on the river. A private boatman and a warm shawl make it perfect for elders.

venues.name: Kirtan & satsang evenings
venues.note: As the aarti ends, the ashrams fill with kirtan, call-and-response devotional singing that builds for hours, and satsang, quiet talks with resident teachers. Sitting in on an evening of music and stillness is the most authentic, least touristed thing you can do in Rishikesh. A guide knows which sessions welcome visitors on any given night.

venues.name: The Ganga at Muni Ki Reti (river ghats)
venues.note: The stretch of clean, swimmable Ganga between the bridges where locals and pilgrims take a holy dip on white-sand shallows, the water cold and glass-clear straight off the mountains. Even a barefoot paddle at the ghats is part of the pilgrimage. Mornings are calmest; a guide points you to the safe, gentle entries for a family.

venues.name: A silent meditation retreat
venues.note: For those who want more than a class, Rishikesh's ashrams run structured silent retreats, days of guided meditation, pranayama and stillness with no phone and no talking, the deepest form of what draws seekers here. Transformative even in a compressed few days. Your advisor arranges the right ashram, comfort level and teacher for a first retreat.

venues.name: The Maa Chandi Devi & Neel Dhara Pakshi Vihar
venues.note: Below the Chandi Devi hill, the Neel Dhara bird sanctuary on a Ganga barrage draws large flocks of migratory waterbirds in winter, an unexpected, tranquil counterpoint to Haridwar's intensity, and a treat for grandparents and birdwatchers. Come in the cool early morning with binoculars. Easily paired with the temple ropeways.

venues.name: Evening at the Triveni Ghat feeding & floating diyas
venues.note: Beyond the aarti itself, dusk at Triveni Ghat is a gentle ritual, feeding the sacred fish in the shallows and setting a leaf-boat lamp adrift on the current with a wish, a quiet moment even small children love. A soft, personal counterpart to the grand ceremonies. Buy a diya from the ghat stalls as the light fades.

venues.name: Riverside cafés & bonfire evenings
venues.note: After the aarti, the town winds down over chai, cold coffee and a Ganga-side rooftop, or a bonfire at a riverside camp upstream.
credentials: Alcohol-free rooftop cafés over the Ganga (Little Buddha, Bistro Nirvana and others)
Bonfire evenings at riverside camps toward Shivpuri
No alcohol served, chai, coffee and conversation
